14.0.s.en: (1) The death of Tobit in a good old age

14.0.0.en: In the last chapter the book summarizes for us the life of St. Tobit the father, who lived fifty-six years in a godly life with God and in good works. Then he was struck with blindness and remained four years in this severe affliction, and at its end his son traveled with the angel Raphael, then returned, married to Sarah, and opened his father's eyes. Tobit was sixty years old when he saw again. Then he lived joyfully with God, with his wife, his son and all his loved ones, and even with his grandchildren, in the fear of God, until he died in a good old age, forty-two years after his sight returned, so that he was then one hundred and two years old, and that was around the year 631 BC. He was buried in the city of Nineveh, honored with great honor by his sons and all his loved ones.

14.1.s.en: (2) Tobit's prophecy of the return from captivity and his last testament

14.1.0.en: Before the death of Tobit the father, he summoned his son Tobias, who had begotten seven sons, and gave them all his last testament, which is full of joyful prophecies for the people of God. And Sarah, who signifies the Church by her marriage to Tobias the son, who signifies Christ, bore seven sons, who signify the seven sacraments of the Church, which Christ gave to His Church.

14.2.0.en: Then he confirmed the words of the prophets, such as Nahum (Nah 3:1), that Nineveh would be utterly destroyed. This was something very strange, because it was the greatest city in the world, being the capital of the Assyrian Empire that ruled the world.

14.2.1.en: This shows the vanity of perishable material powers, so the children of God should not depend on them. Likewise, let no one be deceived by his strength and authority, but let him look to God, the only power that is steadfast in this life and forever, so that he is not troubled by afflictions, or by the threats of others and their domination, but takes refuge in God in everything, even before thinking of his own strength or the strength of those around him. Thus his heart is at peace, in God's hands, under all circumstances.

14.3.0.en: He also proclaimed the return of the people of God from captivity to Jerusalem. For after the Assyrian captivity, in which Tobit was living, the Babylonian captivity would come, and after it the kingdom of the Medes and Persians would arise, at the beginning of which the Jews would return to Jerusalem. He also proclaimed that the city and all Judea would be filled with those who fear God and love to worship Him, for the ruined house of God would be built again, and they would offer in it their sacrifices and their worship to the one God.

14.4.0.en: He even prophesied about the faith of the Gentiles and their rulers, who would exalt Jerusalem, bow down to God in it, worship Him and join His people, leaving the worship of idols.

14.4.1.en: This was not a prophecy only about Jerusalem and the return from captivity, but also about the world's return to the faith and the spread of Christianity everywhere, before the Second Coming of Christ.

14.4.2.en: The Gentiles' return to God would take place through their faith in Christ, as many from the different nations of the world believed.

14.5.0.en: Then Tobit the father continues his last testament, calling his sons to true worship of God from the heart and to care for pleasing Him in all their lives.

14.6.0.en: He also charged them to teach their children to walk uprightly, and to observe justice in all their dealings, so that they would wrong no one. Then he stressed the importance of almsgiving and mercy. And finally, to take care to remember the name of the Lord at all times, to praise Him and to glorify Him, in order to remain in His company and constant fellowship.

14.7.0.en: Then he closed his testament with a specific command, which was to leave the city of Nineveh as soon as his wife Anna died and was buried with him in one tomb, so that they might escape destruction in Nineveh, the great city, which would be destroyed as a result of its many evils.

14.7.1.en: Nineveh signifies the world, which will perish by its iniquity, and therefore the children of God must go out from it, that is, be strangers to its desires and its sins and live for Christ.

14.8.0.en: "Closed their eyes": what those close to the dead do immediately after their death, that is, he was present at their death and burial.

14.8.2.en: Tobias the son took care to carry out his father's testament. A few years after his father was buried, his mother died, and he buried her with honor beside his father. Then he set out with all his sons and grandchildren, taking all his money, and traveled to his parents-in-law, Raguel and Anna, who rejoiced greatly at meeting him and their daughter, and all their children whom they had longed to see. Raguel and Anna had by then become old.

14.8.3.en: Thus the faith of Tobias the son and his obedience to his father are shown, for he abandoned the great city of Nineveh, with all its glory, confident of the truth of his father's word that it would be destroyed.

14.8.4.en: May we obey the commandments of God, however much they conflict with our human wisdom and the thoughts of the world.

14.9.0.en: After God had bestowed many blessings on Tobit the father and the son, He also bestowed them on the righteous Raguel and Anna, for they lived years with the children of their daughter Sarah, and completed their lives in godliness and prayer, rejoicing in the Lord, until they died in a good old age, and Tobias buried them with great honor.

14.9.1.en: Here we see the joy that distinguishes the children of God from the people of the world, this joy that continues throughout their lives, even in the midst of afflictions and in old age, when a person grows weak and the battles of fear, anxiety and complaining increase. But the grace of God preserves their joy for them until the end of their life on earth, so that afterward they may speak with Him in heaven in eternal joy.

14.10.0.en: And Tobias the son lived many days in goodness and righteousness. He saw his grandchildren to the fifth generation, until he died at the age of ninety-nine.

14.11.0.en: His sons, relatives and loved ones continued to live a good life, as a good example in the midst of the world, declaring the name of God.

14.11.1.en: For one of God's blessings on a person is to live many days on earth in the fear of God, and not only that, but also to have righteous offspring who bear witness to God.

14.11.2.en: And so this great book ends with abundant blessings and lasting joy for the righteous children of God, who endured many afflictions and held fast to their faith.

14.11.3.en: A- The prayer of Tobit when he was in affliction (ch. 3:1-6). It includes several meanings, the most important of which are:

14.11.4.en: 1- Submission to God's ordering of events.

14.11.10.en: B- The prayer of Sarah when she was in affliction (ch. 3, 13:22). It includes several meanings, the most important of which are:

14.11.14.en: 4- Asking for the removal of the affliction.

14.11.15.en: 5- Suffering to the point of death.

14.11.16.en: 6- Perplexity over the cause of the affliction, because she:

14.11.18.en: b- Sought marriage in the purity of God.

14.11.21.en: 9- The blessings of affliction and its crowns.

14.11.22.en: 10- God rescues His children from afflictions.

14.11.25.en: C- The prayer of Tobit after his healing (ch. 13). It includes several meanings, the most important of which are:-

14.11.26.en: 1- Glorifying God in word and in deed.

14.11.27.en: 2- God's allowing affliction and giving blessings from it.

14.11.28.en: 3- The responsibility of the children of God to make Him known to the world.

14.11.29.en: 4- Affliction is discipline for our sins.

14.11.30.en: 5- Deliverance from afflictions through God's mercy.

14.11.31.en: 6- A call to repentance and to glorify God.

14.11.32.en: 7- Prophecy of the return from captivity and the glory of Jerusalem, whether through Christ the Savior or in the Kingdom of Heaven.

14.11.33.en: D- A comparison between the prayers of Tobit and Sarah when they were in affliction:

14.11.34.en: There is a great similarity between the two prayers in the following:

14.11.38.en: 4- Suffering to the point of death.

14.11.39.en: 5- Glorifying God and blessing His judgments.

14.11.40.en: E- A comparison between the two prayers of Tobit, when he was in affliction and after his healing from it:- There is a similarity between the two prayers in the following:-

14.11.42.en: 2- Sin is the cause of affliction.

14.11.44.en: But there is a clear difference between them, which is that the first prayer is marked by the suffering of pain and the expectation of death, while the second prayer is marked by thanksgiving, praise, faith in salvation, and a call to the children of God to glorify Him and to enjoy the splendor of Jerusalem.

14.11.45.en: 1- The marriage procedures, which consisted of Raguel, the bride's father, writing the marriage contract, taking his daughter's hand and handing her over to her bridegroom; here he represents the priest of the family (ch. 7:15).

14.11.46.en: 2- The continence of Tobias and Sarah for three days and their prayers (ch. 8:4).

14.11.47.en: 3- Holding the wedding feast in the fear of God (ch. 9:12).

14.11.48.en: 4- The instructions of Sarah's parents to her, with their five contents (ch. 10:13). A summary of the most important characteristics of the angel Raphael

14.11.49.en: 1- He is one of the seven archangels who stand before God at all times (Tob 12:15).

14.11.50.en: 2- He appeared as a guide for the roads of the cities under the name Azariah, in the form of a young man of handsome appearance (Tob 5:5, 6, 18).

14.11.51.en: 3- After showing his readiness to guide Tobias the son to Rages (Tob 5:14, 20), he met Tobit the father to reassure him that he would bring his son there.

14.11.52.en: 4- When the fish attacked Tobias the son, he saved him from it and charged him to take its heart, liver and gall and to salt the rest of its flesh (Tob 6:3, 5).

14.11.53.en: 5- He guided Tobias the son to marry Sarah (Tob 6:12). He reassured Raguel her father and advised Tobias to burn the liver and the heart when he entered the marriage chamber and to abstain from Sarah for three days (Tob 6:

14.11.54.en: 6- During the marriage celebration he went to Gabael in Rages, recovered the loan from him and took him with him, to meet Tobias the son and congratulate him on his marriage (Tob 9).

14.11.55.en: 7- He accompanied Tobias the son on the road back to his father and mother, then divided the procession into two parts, and he and Tobias went ahead to meet his parents and reassure them (Tob 11).

14.11.56.en: 8- When Tobit and his son tried to offer him money, he thanked them and declared to them who he was, that he is the archangel Raphael and that he had been offering up the prayers of Tobit the father and Sarah. The father and his son bowed down before him, and he ascended to heaven (Tob 12). Tobit the father

14.11.57.en: 1- Tobit was a young man of the tribe of Naphtali, who lived in Upper Galilee and was taken captive to the city of Nineveh (Tob 1:1, 3).

14.11.58.en: 2- He was married to a woman of his tribe named Anna, and had by her one son, whom he named after himself (Tob 1:9).

14.11.59.en: 3- He was a righteous man; even as a young man he was diligent in going to the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem to worship and to offer the firstfruits and the tithes, and he did not go to the golden calves that Jeroboam had made (Tob 1:5-7).

14.11.60.en: 4- After his captivity in Nineveh he did not eat of the food of the Gentiles as the rest of the Jews did (Tob 1:12).

14.11.61.en: 5- God gave him favor in the eyes of King Shalmaneser, and he found grace with him, as he worked as purveyor of supplies in the king's palace (Tob 1:13). He used the nature of his work, with its travel throughout the land, to visit his brethren in captivity and remind them of God's commandments (Tob 1:14), and he would help the needy among them, as when he lent ten talents of silver to Gabael, who was in the city of Rages, and took a bond from him for it (ch. 1:16, 17).

14.11.62.en: 6- He took care to bury the dead of the Jews whom the king killed, who persecuted the Jews with great zeal (Tob 1:20), (Tob 2:3, 4), regardless of the reproach of his relatives (Tob 2:8).

14.11.63.en: 7- When King Sennacherib learned of what Tobit was doing in burying the dead, he wanted to kill him, so Tobit fled with his wife and his son, leaving all his money. But God delivered him, for after forty-five days the king's two sons killed him, and Tobit returned to his house and recovered his money (Tob 1:23-25).

14.11.64.en: 8- On one occasion, after burying one of the dead, he returned to his house exhausted and slept beside his house, and the droppings of a bird fell into his eyes and took away his sight (Tob 2:11). He was fifty-six years old (Tob 14:3), and he did not complain despite the reproaches of his wife and his relatives (Tob 2:15-17).

14.11.65.en: 9- His wife was compelled to work at weaving to support the family, after life had become hard for them. Yet, upon hearing the sound of a kid in the house, he feared it might be stolen and warned his wife, who kept reproaching him for his care for God's law, his almsgiving and his hope in God (Tob 2:19-22).

14.11.66.en: 10- When Tobit's need became severe, he summoned his son and informed him of the loan that was with Gabael and asked him to recover it (Tob 4:22). He told him that he had a bond for the money and asked him to take a guide who would show him the way and to give him his wage (Tob 5:3, 4). The son found a young man named Azariah and brought him in to his father, who blessed him, and he set out with his son to travel and recover the loan (Tob 25).

14.11.67.en: 11- He was a man of prayer, who took refuge in God in every matter (Tob 3:1-6, 13).

14.11.68.en: 12- He was a successful father of a family, and he taught his son the commandments of God when he thought he was near death (ch. 4).

14.11.69.en: 13- His hope in God never ceased, and he was certain of His protection of his son Tobias, even when he was late past the time of his return, and he would comfort his wife, assuring her that he would return (Tob 10:6).

14.11.70.en: 14- His son returned after his marriage and the recovery of the loan and anointed his father's eyes with the gall of the fish, and his sight returned to him; he was then sixty years old (Tob 11:13-15).

14.11.71.en: 15- Tobit tried to reward Azariah (the angel Raphael) by giving him half of what his son had brought (Tob 12:5); then Azariah told him the truth of who he was, that he was the angel of the Lord, and he and his son bowed down on the ground and blessed God (Tob 12:11-22).

14.11.72.en: 16- After he regained his sight he lived forty-two years and saw his grandchildren, and he died at the age of one hundred and two and was buried with honor in Nineveh (Tob 14:1, 2), after instructing his son to bury his mother and then leave Nineveh, because it would be destroyed (Tob 14:12). Then he uttered prophecies about the return from captivity, the destruction of Nineveh and the heavenly Jerusalem (Tob 13). Tobias the son

14.11.73.en: 1- He is the only son of Tobit and Anna, who were of the tribe of Naphtali, and he was born in Galilee and was named after his father (Tob 1:1, 9).

14.11.74.en: 2- He helped his father in doing good and in burying the dead; he would tell his father if he saw one of the dead of the children of Israel, and he would invite the godly to his father's feasts (Tob 2:2, 3).

14.11.75.en: 3- He was marked by complete obedience, to the point that he agreed to go and recover the debt without knowing how to do it, and answered his father, "All that you have commanded me I will do" (Tob 5:1); therefore he deserved to be accompanied by an angel.

14.11.76.en: 4- When he went out to look for a guide, the angel of God Raphael met him in the person of Azariah and told him that he had stayed with Gabael in the city of Rages (Tob 5:8), and he went in with Tobias the son to the father and reassured him that he would accompany the son to Gabael and bring the young man back safe (Tob 5:15, 20).

14.11.77.en: 5- Tobias made preparations for the journey and bade his parents farewell; he traveled with his dog, in the company of Azariah, and they reached the river Tigris and spent the night there.

14.11.78.en: 6- When Tobias the son went in to wash in the river, a great fish (a whale) attacked him, and he cried out to Azariah, who commanded him to pull the fish by its gills onto the land. It yielded to him, and he took from it its heart, liver and gall, as the angel commanded him, for uses that would appear later (Tob 16:1-5).

14.11.79.en: 7- Azariah (the angel) guided him to go to Raguel his kinsman and to marry his daughter Sarah, and reassured him that what had befallen her former husbands, who died, would not befall him (Tob 6:11-17).

14.11.80.en: 8- He married Sarah, and when they entered the chamber they burned the fish's liver, and the angel Raphael drove the devil Asmodeus far away from him.

14.11.81.en: 9- Tobias and Sarah kept praying for three nights, and then, after the third night had passed, he was joined to her (Tob 8:

14.11.82.en: 10- Tobias asked the angel to go to Gabael, collect the debt and invite him to his wedding, so that he would not be slow in returning to his father; for he had to remain two weeks in the wedding celebrations, as his father-in-law Raguel requested of him (Tob 8:23; Tob 9:1-5).

14.11.83.en: 11- Tobias loved his parents, so he could not grant Raguel's request that he remain with him more than the two weeks, and he knew how anxious they were. So he took his wife and half of Raguel's possessions, which he gave him, of servants, cattle and maidservants, and traveled back to his parents (Tob 10:8-10).

14.11.84.en: 12- When he reached Haran, which is midway on the road to Nineveh, he left his wife and the caravan in order to hasten to meet his parents (Tob 11:1-3).

14.11.85.en: 13- When he met his father he took out the gall of the fish and anointed his eyes with it, as the angel had charged him, and the father regained his sight (Tob 11:13).

14.11.86.en: 14- He asked his father to reward Azariah (the angel) for all that he had done, and then the angel declared to them who he was, and they bowed down before him (Tob 12:15-22).

14.11.87.en: 15- God granted him seven sons. He buried his father in Nineveh as he had charged him. And after his mother died and was buried beside his father, he took his wife and his sons and left Nineveh, according to his father's testament, and went to his parents-in-law.

14.11.88.en: 16- God blessed him and he saw his sons' sons to the fifth generation, and he buried his parents-in-law and took all their possessions, then died in the fear of the Lord, having completed ninety-nine years (Tob 14:5, 14-16). Sarah

14.11.89.en: 1- She is Sarah the daughter of Raguel and Anna, who lived in the city of Rages in Media (Tob 3:7).

14.11.90.en: 2- She had been married to seven men, one after another. A devil named Asmodeus would kill her husbands when they went in to her (Tob 3:8).

14.11.91.en: 3- She suffered from the reproaches of her maidservant, and she offered fervent prayers and many fasts to God (Tob 3:9-25).

14.11.92.en: 4- Tobias the son came forward to marry her, according to the counsel of Azariah (the angel). And Raguel agreed, despite his fear that what had befallen her previous husbands would befall Tobias (Tob 7:10-13).

14.11.93.en: 5- She and Tobias remained in prayer for three nights, that God might bless them, and after that they were joined in holy marriage, after Tobias had burned the fish's liver, and the angel seized the devil who had been causing the death of her previous husbands (Tob 8:2-7).

14.11.94.en: 6- She left her father's house with her husband Tobias, after the wedding feast, which lasted two weeks (Tob 8:23). Her father gave her half of his possessions, of servants and cattle, and her parents charged her to honor her parents-in-law, love her husband and care for her household (Tob 10:10-13).

14.11.95.en: 7- She reached her parents-in-law a week after her husband's arrival, and they received her with joy and made her a feast for seven days.

14.11.96.en: 8- She bore seven sons, and after sharing with her husband in burying her parents-in-law she left Nineveh.

14.11.97.en: 9- She went with her husband to her parents and lived with them until their death, and she saw her grandchildren.

14.11.98.en: Symbols of Christ and the Church. Tobit signifies Christ. Tobias the son signifies Christ in the following:

14.11.99.en: 1- Tobias had his father's name, just as Christ has the name of His Father, being called Emmanuel, that is, God with us.

14.11.100.en: 2- He did the same works as his father, which are works of mercy and burying the dead, and Christ went about everywhere doing good, like His Father, the Giver of good things.

14.11.101.en: 3- He traveled with the angel serving him and bringing him to his bride Sarah, and Christ became incarnate and the angels serve Him, to redeem His bride, the Church.

14.11.102.en: 4- Satan attacked him in the form of the fish and in the form of the devil Asmodeus, at his marriage, and Tobias triumphed over him. And Christ triumphed over Satan, in the temptation on the mountain and on the cross, when He bound him.

14.11.103.en: 5- He married Sarah, who was tormented and found no rest with the seven husbands who were killed. And Christ married the Church, which did not find its salvation by all the ways in the Old Testament, but obtained salvation through Christ in the New Testament.

14.11.104.en: 6- Raguel dug a grave for Tobias, because he believed he was among the dead, but the maidservant found him alive with his bride and gave Raguel and his wife the good news that they were alive. And Christ entered the tomb but rose, and Magdalene announced His resurrection.

14.11.105.en: 7- Tobias was joined to Sarah and remained with her three days in prayer and continence, then was united with her, to beget sons on the third day. And Christ was joined to His Church and bore her sins on the cross, and on the third day rose from the dead, to give her new life and to beget from her many sons by faith, who are the sons of the New Testament.

14.11.106.en: 8- Tobias recovered the debt from Gabael and gave him back the bond. And Christ paid the debt that was against us by His blood on the cross and offered us salvation.

14.11.107.en: 9- Tobias's parents-in-law tried to keep him with them longer, with his bride, in their house, but he insisted on returning to his father. And Christ ascended to His Father despite His disciples' attachment to Him.

14.11.108.en: 10- Tobias reached his father with the angel and gave him the news of his marriage, and after seven days Sarah arrived. And Christ ascended to heaven with the angels, to prepare a place for His Church, that is, His faithful children, whom He received after Him in Paradise.

14.11.109.en: 11- Tobias healed his father's eyes by placing his hand with the gall upon them. And Christ healed the sick by touching them, such as putting clay on the eyes of the man born blind, and he saw.
